note: Hand truth for the .eml sources under eml/, one entry per source, read from the source as a mail reader would: headers decoded from their encoded words and charsets, times in UTC, each body part decoded from its transfer encoding and charset. Line breaks are written as \n: the source's CRLF is MIME's canonical line break, and the CRLF before a boundary belongs to the boundary. A field the source doesn't have is left out. charset is the text parts' charset where it isn't ASCII. date is the Date header; received the date of the first Received header. A recipient with no display name has only an address. Attachments are in the source's order: the decoded content's size and lowercase hex SHA-256, its filename, content type, Content-ID without angle brackets, and whether its disposition is inline. embedded holds each attached message/rfc822, in this same shape. What each generated format carries of this is the tests' to state: tests/generated.rs.

items_note: Hand truth for the item sources under items/, one entry per source, as the store holds each item: written field by field, not mapped from MIME. class is the message class. The sender and each recipient are a display name and an address. The times are in UTC: for a conversation, submit_time is its start and delivery_time its end, when the history was saved; the creation and modification times are the delivery time. html is the stored HTML body, the item's only body, a Skype for Business IM transcript for a conversation, one line per message with its speaker, time and text; markdown is the Markdown the CLI makes from it. The people and their chats are invented. What the store carries beyond this is the tests' to state: tests/generated.rs.
